chunk_findings.detail: The caller computes `author_model, _ = _author_model(st, agent, "", cfg)` and discards the second returned value, which is the author family. But the helper only passes `author_model` to `GD.review_tier(cfg, author_model, r.model, r.family)`; it never passes the author’s family. If the session model is missing but `[agent].family` is known (e.g. author family is `deepseek` with no session model), `_author_model` returns an empty `author_model`, so `review_tier` cannot know the author’s family. With reviewers `[lan-deepseek-v4-pro(same family), grok-4.7(cross family)]`, both rank as `"none"` (rank 2), the stable sort preserves config order, and the slow same-family reviewer still runs before the fast cross-family reviewer—the exact B19066e802f failure—despite a known author family.

chunk_findings.detail: After exhausted is shed, config [slow same-family, exhausted, fast cross-family] becomes [fast, slow], and the new test requires both to be invoked (`invited == ["fast", "slow"]`). This change only stable-sorts the pool; it never drops or stops on the remaining same-family reviewer once the cross-family one has already served. Sequential dispatch therefore still blocks the gate on lan-deepseek-v4-pro (~9 min) after grok-4.7 returns, so the motivating case stays ~10 min, not ~1-2. Within the cross-family tier the same stable sort also leaves an unmarked 429 reviewer that appears earlier in config (kimi/gemini) ahead of the healthy one, so that reviewer is still waited on before grok serves.
chunk_findings.title: _order_cross_family_first / test_cross_family_first_and_degraded_shed_before_any_attempt

chunk_findings.detail: The cold-gate assertion only requires `fast` to run before `slow`. The `exhausted` reviewer is also cross-family (`moonshot` vs the author family `deepseek`) and appears before `fast` in the config. So an incomplete fix that merely stable-sorts all cross-family reviewers ahead of same-family reviewers would cold-run `exhausted` first and produce `["exhausted", "fast", "slow"]`; this assertion still passes even though the healthy `fast` reviewer did not run first and the 429d reviewer is still attempted before it. The regression test therefore does not pin the stated requirement that a fast cross-family reviewer runs first.
